parts.title: SPIRAL REVIEW (5 min)
content: 1. GRAMMAR SPIRAL: Identify what is WRONG with this conclusion: 'In conclusion, my topic is dolphins. Dolphins are smart. Also, there are many types of dolphins. Additionally, researchers study dolphins in Hawaii.' (Answer: introduces new info, uses 'also / additionally' wrong, no restatement of thesis)
2. CONCLUSION PRACTICE: Write a 3-sentence mini-conclusion for this topic: 'School uniforms should be mandatory.' Use: 'In conclusion...' + summary + restate + call to action.
3. MATH SPIRAL: Your conclusion will reference a key statistic. Find the MOST impactful number from your research. Write it in your conclusion as a 'final thought' sentence.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  The conclusion is your final opportunity to make an impression on your reader. A weak conclusion just repeats the introduction word-for-word. A powerful conclusion does three things: it SUMMARIZES, it RESTATES, and it CALLS TO ACTION.
content: 📖 The conclusion is your final opportunity to make an impression on your reader. A weak conclusion just repeats the introduction word-for-word. A powerful conclusion does three things: it SUMMARIZES, it RESTATES, and it CALLS TO ACTION.
First, SUMMARIZE the key findings from your body paragraphs. Briefly remind the reader of the most important evidence you presented. Use different words from your body paragraphs — do not copy.
Second, RESTATE your thesis. This is your main argument, expressed in new language. It should feel like the logical endpoint of all your evidence.

Third, END WITH IMPACT. This might be a CALL TO ACTION ('Therefore, governments and individuals must...'), a FINAL THOUGHT ('Ultimately, our actions today will determine...'), or a QUESTION TO THE READER ('What will you do to help solve this problem?').
A conclusion should NEVER introduce new ideas or new evidence. Everything in the conclusion should come from what you already discussed.
(↑ Re-read the story above to answer:)
